Notice Made Under Primary Legislation

Where possible, actual verified emissions data is preferable to use for UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). However, default values are available to ensure liable persons can comply with CBAM, even where actual reported emissions data is not available. The government’s guiding principle in setting default values is to protect the environmental integrity of the CBAM and ensure that there is no advantage to liable persons in using default values, rather than determining the actual embodied emissions of imported CBAM goods.

Default values for UK CBAM are based on EU data, which was calculated to reflect the same CBAM system boundaries as the UK. The UK’s default values have been set on a trade-weighted average basis, meaning the values reflect the composition of UK imports. Data from the EU is excluded. This helps to ensure the values better reflect the emissions embodied in goods for which the default values are most likely to be used, as well as recognising the commitment expressed by the UK and EU to link their emissions trading schemes which will result in EU-origin goods being exempt from UK CBAM.

A markup on default values helps to balance supporting the objectives of the CBAM and facilitating a transition to actual emissions reporting. On that basis, a markup of 10% has been applied in all sectors except fertiliser, where no markup is applied.

These default values will be in force from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2028. From 2029, the UK will move to country-specific default values, with one default value per CBAM good per country. This will help to provide a more granular and accurate reflection of the emissions embodied in CBAM goods. The appropriate level of markup will be reviewed at this time.

These default values will be updated in due course as necessary to account for any future changes to the Combined Nomenclature system.

The following text has the force of law by virtue of paragraph 11(1) of Schedule 17 to the Finance Act 2026.
